assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created a controllable, strongly coupled light-matter platform with superconducting artificial atoms and microwave resonators. It enabled dispersive readout, quantum nondemolition measurement and multi-qubit gates, and underlies most present superconducting quantum processors. Originality and lasting impact are very high. I declare my own field proximity (superconducting circuits, WACQT) and have tried to judge strictly on the merits.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal by Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf and the first experiments by the Yale group are the decisive core. Theory (Blais, Girvin) and experiment (Schoelkopf) form a natural split, but the supplied credit omits Andreas Wallraff, whose experimental contribution was central, and others, so the three-name configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over two decades and now industrial-scale; the interpretation is completely stable. Recognition is timely, although the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely related and may argue for waiting a few years.
uncertainties: Wallraff's omission from the supplied names and the allocation among up to five key contributors are unresolved.
Proximity to the 2025 prize may weigh against a second circuit-based award soon.
I cannot independently verify exact priority details of the 2004 proposal versus the 2004 experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and laid out how to realize quantum computation and simulation with ions and neutral atoms. These ideas shaped two major experimental platforms and the field of quantum simulation. Originality and conceptual clarity are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: A compact and widely recognised two-person theory pairing. The 1995 ion gate proposal was joint, and the cold-atom (Jaksch et al.) work was Zoller-led with Cirac contributions. Experimental pioneers such as Wineland and Blatt are not in this entry; Wineland already has a prize, which strengthens the case for theory recognition.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally validated for many years across ions and neutral atoms, with commercial systems now in operation. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether a theory-only prize is preferred over one including experimental groups.
Overlap with other candidates crediting Zoller means these entries may compete for the same laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 launched quantum cryptography and information-theoretic security grounded in quantum mechanics. It is a foundational idea connected to Bell tests and quantum communication, with deployed networks and satellite links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84 and have credit for the broader framework; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is independent and important. The two-name configuration is defensible, but omitting Ekert will be contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental demonstration, from fibre to satellite; the concept is stable. Practical security implementation issues remain but do not affect the scientific discovery.
uncertainties: Fair treatment of Ekert versus Bennett and Brassard.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments may be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity by Jarillo-Herrero's group opened the twistronics field and moire quantum matter. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: A clear theory-experiment pairing, with MacDonald and Bistritzer as theory authors of the continuum model and Jarillo-Herrero leading the experimental discovery. Cao and colleagues are co-authors on the experiments and other theory groups contributed; the best three-person configuration is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely in many groups and platforms, although the mechanism of superconductivity and many correlated phases remain debated. Recognition is plausible but the physics is still evolving.
uncertainties: Credit among first-author experimentalists and theory contributors is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept with magic wavelengths (Katori) and its realisation to the 10^-18 level (Ye and others) transformed time and frequency metrology and enabled tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye led demonstrations of record precision. Hall and Hansch were already recognised for combs, and trapped-ion clocks (Wineland) are separate. Credit is fairly clean for two names.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation at several institutes; redefinition of the second is in progress, which signals maturity. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an extension of previously recognised comb and ion-clock work.
Contributions of other clock groups are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological invariant, with the Molenkamp-group observation in HgTe wells, established topological insulators as a major field with lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal; Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang predicted HgTe and Konig et al. observed it, so credit also depends on those names, who are not in this entry. The listed trio is a plausible but incomplete configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in 2D and 3D, and with ARPES; applications are still limited. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions is related, so novelty relative to it should be weighed.
uncertainties: Omission of Zhang and Bernevig and of 3D topological insulator pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological quantum error correction and surface codes provide the leading route to fault-tolerant quantum computing. Kitaev's toric code and anyon-based ideas are conceptually deep. Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold operation are recent. I note my interest in error correction through WACQT.
assessment.attribution: Kitaev proposed the toric code; Bravyi and Kitaev developed surface codes and Preskill, Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl and Raussendorf contributed to thresholds. Credit is diffuse and several decisive contributors may be missing.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is recent and the full fault-tolerant payoff is not yet realised, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kitaev, Bravyi, Preskill, Dennis and Raussendorf is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, quantum gas microscopes and fermionic Hubbard physics, created a new experimental route to strongly correlated matter.
assessment.attribution: Greiner, Bloch and Hansch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger led fermionic studies; Zoller and Jaksch proposed the scheme. Experimentalists are credited here, but the theory proposal remains a point of fairness since Zoller overlaps with B015.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely replicated, with analog quantum simulators now in broad use. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Whether Zoller should be paired with experimentalists or kept to B015.
Several other groups are not credited in the supplied entry.
